chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him) describing the one who walks the path to God, Exalted is He.

He who is patient prevails, he who is ignorant is incapacitated, he who is lazy perishes, he who is greedy has bad opinion of God, he who is content is pleased with God, he who relies on God God suffices him, he who is grateful God increases him, he who remains silent is safe, he whose character is good is loved by people, and he whose character is bad is disliked by people.
ai.seo_question: What are the key spiritual qualities of a seeker of God according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha outlines the spiritual and social qualities of the seeker of God, contrasting negative traits like impatience, ignorance, and greed with positive virtues such as patience, contentment, and good character. It links internal states to external outcomes and divine support, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the unity of inner piety (taqwa) and outward conduct. The description serves as a practical guide for the Sufi-like path of self-purification (tazkiyah) within the broader framework of Islamic ethics.
